title: Figma
objectives: Understand Figma via a real-life analogy
Master Auto Layout + Components + Variants + Variables
Hand off designs to Flutter engineers efficiently

sections.markdown:
**Think of Figma as a collaborative shared Google Doc for design.**

Everyone works in the same file simultaneously — designers, PMs, engineers, brand — with instant multiplayer editing + comments + version history. Unlike Sketch (macOS-only, file-based) or Photoshop (single-user, pixel-based), Figma is browser + vector + realtime.

- **Frames** — artboards; each screen (Home, Cart, Checkout).
- **Auto Layout** — flexbox for design; children arrange themselves.
- **Components** — reusable master widgets; edit master → all instances update.
- **Variants** — same component with state variations (button primary/secondary/disabled).
- **Variables** — design tokens (colors, spacings, typography) linked across the file.
- **Prototyping** — link frames + define animations.
- **Dev Mode** — engineer-focused view: inspect measurements + copy code hints + auto-generated Flutter snippets (via plugins).

**Why every Flutter team's design surface is Figma:** engineers open the same file the designer used; measurements match exactly; component library reflects Flutter's widget library. When the design system is Figma-first + tokens sync to Flutter, entire screens can be built without pixel-pushing.

**Figma** is a browser-based collaborative UI/UX design tool. Vector-based; supports Auto Layout (flexbox-like), Components (reusable widgets), Variants (component states), Variables (design tokens for colors/typography/spacing), Prototyping, Dev Mode, Comments, Version History, Plugins. Companion products: **FigJam** (whiteboarding), **Figma Slides**, **Figma Sites**.

sections.markdown: ## Figma → Flutter token sync
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Frames without Auto Layout.** Manual positioning breaks on translation + copy changes. Auto Layout everywhere.
**Mistake 2: Components without Variants.** 8 similar buttons duplicated → editing 1 doesn't propagate. Consolidate as one component + variants.
**Mistake 3: Hard-coded colors + spacings.** Change brand color → hundreds of edits. Use Variables from day one.
**Mistake 4: No shared library.** Every project has its own components; drift + inconsistency. Publish a team library.
**Mistake 5: Ignoring Dev Mode.** Engineers eyeball measurements. Dev Mode → exact code snippets + tokens + measurements.
**Mistake 6: Off-grid pixel-pushing.** 8pt-grid discipline breaks; Auto Layout + tokens enforce it.
**Mistake 7: No mobile + tablet + desktop frames** — engineer scrambles for breakpoints.
**Mistake 8: Prototypes not updated with dev implementation.** Users test outdated flows.
## Best practices
**1. Auto Layout for every Frame.**
**2. Components + Variants** for every reusable pattern.
**3. Variables for tokens** — color, spacing, radius, type ramp.
**4. Shared library** published to the org.
**5. 8pt grid + explicit spacing tokens.**
**6. Multi-breakpoint frames** — mobile / tablet / desktop.
**7. Dev Mode integration** — plugin export → Flutter tokens.
**8. Prototypes updated as source of truth** for engineering interactions.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Login screen with Auto Layout + button component.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Button component with 4 variants (primary/secondary/tertiary/danger).
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Color + spacing + type Variables for a small app.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Export tokens → generate Dart ThemeData.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Multi-breakpoint responsive prototype.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Design system library with 20+ components; publish + version.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Why Auto Layout matters + when do you NOT use it?**

**A:** **Auto Layout** is Figma's flexbox equivalent — children arrange themselves based on direction (horizontal/vertical), spacing, padding, resize behavior. **Wins:** (1) copy changes don't break layout — text grows, siblings shift. (2) Translations don't require manual repositioning. (3) Design mirrors implementation — Flutter's Row + Column + Padding + spacing map 1:1. (4) Component variants swap cleanly. **When NOT to use:** (1) Truly free-form illustrations (hero images, decorative art) where spatial relationships are creative, not systematic. (2) Icon glyph internals. (3) Absolute-position overlays (badges, notification dots — use constraints + position). **Rule:** structural UI = Auto Layout; illustrations = free-form. Interviewer signal: knowing WHEN not to use it separates advanced from beginner.

**Q2: How would you sync Figma design tokens to Flutter?**

**A:** **Pattern:** (1) Define tokens in Figma **Variables** — color, spacing, radius, type ramp. Modes for light/dark. (2) Export via **Figma REST API** or a plugin (Tokens Studio, Figma to Flutter). (3) Emit `tokens.json` — versioned in git alongside Flutter code. (4) A build step reads `tokens.json` + generates `brand_tokens.dart` with typed constants + a `ThemeData` factory. (5) Flutter uses `Theme.of(context)` for anything themable. (6) CI regenerates on token changes; PR review + tests catch regressions. **Bidirectional flow trap:** engineers hand-edit `brand_tokens.dart` → out-of-sync with Figma. **Solution:** tokens.dart is generated + gitignored; designers own the source of truth. Interviewer signal: automating the sync + owning the source of truth.

**Q3: How do Variants + Interactive Components help engineers?**

**A:** **Variants** consolidate 'similar-but-different' component instances — a Button component with `{state: primary/secondary, size: sm/md/lg, disabled: true/false}` = 12 combinations from ONE master. Engineer sees exactly what states exist; no confusion about 'is there a hover?' — Figma lists all variant properties. **Interactive Components** allow states to CHANGE on interaction inside Figma (hover expands; toggle switches). Engineer can PROTOTYPE the interaction flow in the design without a mockup video. **Result:** the design file becomes an executable spec. Flutter engineer maps variants to conditional rendering / state; there's no ambiguity. **Trap:** Variants that don't match Flutter state model (e.g., Figma has 'hover' but Flutter mobile doesn't) — align vocab with engineering.

**Q4: What's the Dev Mode workflow?**

**A:** **Dev Mode** (paid Figma feature, but standard for teams) is a view designed for engineers: (1) Select any layer → panel shows measurements, colors (with hex + token reference), typography, spacing, radius. (2) Auto-generated code snippets — CSS, iOS SwiftUI, Android Compose, and via plugins Flutter. (3) Component inspector — 'this is a Button variant primary/lg' — no guessing. (4) Section-based export — 'download the icons for this screen.' (5) Ready-for-dev sections marked by designers → engineer's queue. (6) Comments per-layer for questions. (7) Version history diff for 'what changed since sprint start?' **Trade-off:** Dev Mode is a paid feature; small teams share designer-Editor seats + get less integrated experience. **Interviewer signal:** knowing Dev Mode's value + which plugins bridge to Flutter (e.g., FigmaToCode, Locofy, Anima).

**Q5: How would you organize a Figma file for a multi-screen Flutter app?**

**A:** **(1) One file per major project** (Consumer app, Admin dashboard); split when it grows unwieldy. **(2) Pages inside the file:** `Design System` (components + tokens), `iOS`, `Android`, `Web`, `Explorations` (WIP), `Archive`. **(3) Each screen as a Frame** at target device size. **(4) Cover page** — table of contents + status per screen. **(5) Components published from `Design System` page to a team library** — reused across files. **(6) Variables shared across files** via a Variables library. **(7) Prototype flows** grouped per user journey (login, checkout, settings). **(8) Comments used liberally** for open questions + hand-off notes. **(9) Version snapshots** at end of each sprint. **(10) Named layers** — engineers hate `Rectangle 47`. Interviewer signal: file hygiene matters at team scale.

**Q6: How would you introduce Figma to a Flutter team that's been using PDFs / screenshots?**

**A:** **(1) Start with a real project** — one feature, not the whole app. **(2) Migrate the design system first** — 20 components + tokens; engineers see the value immediately. **(3) Pair a designer + engineer** — Figma-native handoff replaces email attachments. **(4) Introduce Dev Mode** — measurements + tokens visible. **(5) Automate token export** — generate Dart file; commit to Flutter repo. **(6) Set up naming conventions** — screens, components, tokens. **(7) Publish a team library** — org-wide reuse. **(8) Training** — designer teaches engineers Figma basics (30 min); engineer teaches designer Flutter constraints. **(9) Onboarding docs** — 'how we use Figma.' **(10) Measure adoption** — velocity of design-to-code shortens, rework drops. **Culture win:** designer + engineer speak the same language + iterate together. Interviewer signal: rollout as change management, not just tool intro.

## Real-world usage

- **Every professional Flutter product team** — Figma is default.
- **Design systems** — Material 3 kit, brand libraries.
- **Rapid prototyping** — user testing sessions.
- **Design-to-code plugins** — Locofy, Anima, FigmaToCode.
- **NOT ideal for** — pixel-perfect illustrations (use Illustrator); highly technical diagrams (Excalidraw).

## Advanced notes

- **Auto Layout modes** — horizontal / vertical / wrap (2024+).
- **Variables modes** — light/dark, brand A / brand B.
- **Component properties** — instances swap without breaking layout.
- **Nested instances** — swap sub-components inside a Master.
- **Slots** — placeholder for content in Interactive Components.
- **Advanced prototyping** — expressions + conditional flow.
- **Figma REST API** — full read/write; auto-export via CI.
- **Widgets** — Figma canvas mini-apps (polls, timers).
- **Community files** — massive library of open designs.
- **Version history + branches** — sprint-based collaboration.
- **Section vs Frame** — Section groups Frames; better organization.
- **Component playground** — interactive component instances for stakeholder demos.
- **Design linter plugins** — enforce token usage.
- **FigJam integration** — brainstorm + flow → design.
- **Figma Slides** — presentations in Figma.
- **Figma Sites** — publish designs as live websites.
- **AI in Figma (2024+)** — image gen, auto-complete.
